name: Baked Pumpkin Kibbeh
steps: Cook the pumpkin until tender, then drain it very well and mash to measure 600 g; wet pumpkin makes the crust weak. Rinse the fine bulgur briefly and squeeze out excess water. Mix it with the mashed pumpkin, semolina, warm water, 4 g salt and allspice. Knead for 5 minutes into a cohesive orange dough and rest covered for 20 minutes so the bulgur softens.

Heat 20 ml olive oil in a wide pan. Cook the diced onion for 5 minutes, then add chopped spinach and cook 3–4 minutes until wilted. Press off excess liquid. Stir in drained chickpeas, chopped walnuts, lemon juice, sumac and 4 g salt. Cook 2 minutes and cool completely; the filling should be moist but not runny.

Heat the oven to 200°C and oil a roughly 24 cm round baking tin with 10 ml olive oil. With damp hands press half the pumpkin-bulgur dough evenly across the base, about 1 cm thick. Spread the cooled spinach-chickpea filling over it, leaving a small clear border around the rim.

Flatten the remaining pumpkin dough in small pieces between damp palms and place over the filling, then join the pieces gently into an even top layer without squeezing out the filling. Score the top into four to eight portions with a knife. Brush with the remaining 25 ml olive oil and sprinkle with the remaining 1 g salt.

Bake for 35–40 minutes until the top is firm, richly golden and lightly crisp at the edges. Rest 15 minutes before cutting along the scored lines. Serve warm with lemon wedges; each portion should show orange pumpkin-bulgur layers around a distinct green spinach, chickpea and walnut centre.
tips: Use fine bulgur rather than coarse bulgur and squeeze the cooked pumpkin dry. The reviewed photo shows a tray-baked, cut layered kibbeh with a golden pumpkin-bulgur crust and visible spinach, chickpeas and walnuts; it is not a meat croquette.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
